'''''Sisyrinchium bermudiana''''', known as '''Bermudiana'''<ref name="GovBermuda"/>  or, along with other members of the genus, as '''blue-eyed grass''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |access-date=2014-10-17}}</ref> is a flower of the genus ''[[Sisyrinchium]]'' (of the [[Iridaceae|Iris family]]) that is native to the [[Atlantic Ocean|Atlantic]] [[archipelago]], and [[British Overseas Territory]], of [[Bermuda]] and the island of [[Ireland]]. The plant appears and blooms in the spring. It is used as a national flower by Bermudians, and appears in art, jewellery, banknotes and elsewhere.<ref name="GovBermuda">{{cite web |title=Bermudiana |url=https://environment.bm/bermudiana |website=Government of Bermuda - Department of the Environment and Natural Resources |access-date=27 March 2026}}</ref>

==Description==
The plant has green to greyish-green strap-like basal leaves. In spring the flowers appear, six purple-blue perianth segments, joined into a central yellow coloured tube, from which the 3 stamens protrude, along with a 3-lobed style. The ovary is inferior. There are several flowers in a group on each branched flower stem.<ref name="Rose&O'Reilly2006">{{cite book |last1=Rose |first1=Francis |last2=O'Reilly |first2=Claire |title=The Wild Flower Key |date=2006 |publisher=Frederick Warne, Penguin Group |location=London |isbn=9780723251750 |page=517 |edition=2nd}}</ref> The seed pods are dark in colour and release many small round black seeds.<ref name="GovBermuda" />

==Taxonomy==
''Sisyrinchium bermudiana'' was first described by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1753.<ref name="IPNI_440950-1">{{citation |title=IPNI Plant Name Details for ''Sisyrinchium bermudiana'' |work=[[International Plant Names Index|The International Plant Names Index]] |url=http://www.ipni.org/ipni/idPlantNameSearch.do;?id=440950-1 |accessdate=2015-04-27 }}</ref> The first described species in the genus ''Sisyrinchium'', it is thus the [[type species]]. Linnaeus's specific epithet ''bermudiana'' was not an adjective (and thus does not have to agree in gender with ''Sisyrinchium'') but a noun in apposition, derived from the earlier genus name ''Bermudiana''.<ref name=Linn53/> He showed this by capitalizing the epithet, but modern practice is to use lower-case for all epithets.

==Distribution and habitat==
Its distribution, in the Atlantic archipelago, Bermuda and Ireland, has led to the suggestion that it was introduced to Ireland, rather than being endemic. There are no records of it in Ireland before 1845.<ref name="Stace2019">{{cite book |last1=Stace |first1=Clive |title=New Flora of the British Isles |date=2019 |publisher=C&M Floristics |location=Suffolk |isbn=9781527226302 |page=927 |edition=Fourth}}</ref>

It grows in sandy areas, wet meadows, near lakes and coastal forest floors, but is also grown widely as a garden ornamental. It will spread by self-seeding to cover the ground.<ref name="Stace2019" /><ref name="GovBermuda" />
